name: Question 9
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=2x(t)+3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are ${v}_{1}=[-1,\text{ }1]^{T}$ and ${v}_{2}=[-1,\text{ }2]^{T},$ respectively. Select the correct options below regarding the given system.$\,$
$y=-x$ is {{field-1}} line.

$\,$
{{field-2}} is {{field-3}} line.

$\,$
The equilibrium point (origin) is {{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
The general solution of the system is

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]={c}_{1}{e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=-x$ is $\text{an unstable}$ line.

- The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y=-2x.
$$

The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{2t}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line and approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, $y=-2x$ is $\text{an unstable}$ line.

Therefore, the equilibrium point (origin) is $\text{an unstable node (source)}.$
